text: Codex has no two-in-a-row loop guard, because it ends the turn itself at the first reply that reaches the model's output limit, so that failure is its loop guard's stop, refining D-0151 (#374). codex-cli 0.163.0 takes the Responses API's incomplete response, reason max_output_tokens, as an error it never retries, so codex exec emits an error event and then turn.failed, each saying "Incomplete response returned, reason: max_output_tokens", and exits 1; its events don't say what the reply held. A Codex attempt whose failed turn, or else its last error event, gives that reason stops as the loop guard's stop, never as its provider's failure, and the build runs it once more at -fallback-effort, as when Claude Code's guard stops a run: xhigh by default, and medium on @gitdek's watchers, as D-0174 set. A fallback run that fails the same way fails the build with Codex's reason, and the build says it fell back and why. A provider's failure never takes the fallback. Claude Code's guard, two replies in a row of nothing but thinking, is unchanged.
